title: The wedding feast
hook: a meal to celebrate, even with one sheep (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the mahr, the bride's own free gift. Your line: hers alone.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf walks into Medina with a trace of yellow on his clothes, the color of a perfume, and the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ notices. What's this? I've married a woman of the Ansar, he says. The Prophet asks what he gave her. A date stone's weight of gold. Then the Prophet tells him the next thing to do. Not buy a house. Not throw a party to impress the town. In Sahih al-Bukhari, his words come down to this: hold a wedding meal, even if it's only one sheep. The marriage is made. Now feed people. Today's word: walimah.
screen: `A TRACE OF YELLOW ON HIS CLOTHES.` → `I'VE MARRIED.` → `HOLD A MEAL, EVEN WITH ONE SHEEP.`

segments.voice: Walimah is the wedding feast, the meal that celebrates and announces a marriage. The nikah needed a public celebration; this is it, served on plates. First, the size. Even one sheep. The point isn't the menu. It's that there should be a meal at all, shared, so the marriage is known and the joy is passed around. Second, what a feast can look like. In Bukhari, the companion Anas describes a wedding meal the Prophet gave with no bread and no meat at all: dates, dried yogurt and butter, spread on a leather mat. Third, who's at the table. A report in Bukhari, from Abu Hurayrah, is blunt: the worst food is the food of a wedding feast where the rich are invited and the poor are left out. The walimah can be humble. What it can't be, in that report, is a party that shuts the door on the poor. Fourth, the guests' side. Bukhari also keeps the instruction that when someone is invited to a wedding feast, they should come. Showing up is part of it. The schools discuss how strong these are: whether holding a walimah is required or strongly recommended, and when a guest may excuse himself. A marriage is made with words. Then it's celebrated with food, and the guest list reaches past the people who can invite you back. The feast tells the town these two are married, and it turns a private joy into something a neighbor can taste.
screen: `EVEN ONE SHEEP.` · `DATES AND BUTTER ON A LEATHER MAT.` · `THE WORST FOOD: RICH IN, POOR OUT.` · `WHEN YOU'RE INVITED, COME.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind the best meal you ever shared, not the most expensive, the best: who was at the table, and what was on it? Notice how much of the memory is the food and how much is the people. Then picture a simple table for one small good thing that hasn't been celebrated, and one person you'd invite who's rarely invited; if you pray, you can give thanks in your own words.
Walimah. The wedding feast, held to celebrate and announce a marriage, even if it's only one sheep, with the poor at the table too. Today's word.
Your line: feed people. Even one sheep, even dates on a leather mat, with the poor invited. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: After a nikah, a Muslim family may hold a walimah, a wedding meal for relatives, friends and neighbors, which may be a simple dinner at home or a large hall reception; guests who are invited are encouraged to attend.

chat.says: Does a Muslim wedding feast have to be big and expensive to count?
options: No. Even one sheep, or dates on a mat; share it, and invite the poor.
Yes. A small feast doesn't count; it should impress the whole town.
Only if the guests are family and friends who can invite you back.
chat.meaning: Hold a meal, even if it's only one sheep. The worst wedding food, a report says, is where the rich are invited and the poor left out.
